name: obra/superpowers — 249K Stars; Official Claude Marketplace; Agentic Skills Framework That Refuses to Write Code First
hook: Jesse Vincent's obra/superpowers is the most-starred Claude Code plugin on GitHub at 249K — and it earned those stars by doing something counterintuitive: refusing to write code until it has fully designed the solution first. The 14 skills install a structured dev methodology: design refinement → test-driven development → subagent-driven implementation → code review → git worktree coordination. No immediate code dumps. Simon Willison called Jesse 'one of the most creative users of coding agents I know.' Simon Scrapes' video '14 GENIUS Ways to Give Claude Code SUPERPOWERS' likely drove a significant share of the growth. Official listing at claude.com/plugins/superpowers; v6.1.1 released July 2, 2026. Three-repo ecosystem: superpowers, superpowers-marketplace, superpowers-lab.

name: Claude Code v2.1.202 — Dynamic Workflow Size Setting; Fixed Duplicate Skill Loading; /review Reverted to Single-Pass
hook: v2.1.202 shipped July 6 with one headline feature and one critical fix: The /config now has a 'Dynamic workflow size' toggle (small/medium/large) that advises how many agents to spawn per workflow — useful for keeping costs predictable on Max plans. The critical fix: re-invoking an already-loaded skill no longer appended a full duplicate copy of its instructions every time — a context-bleeding bug that inflated token costs on any session that called a skill more than once. Also: /review <pr#> is now back to a fast single-pass review (the multi-agent version moved to /code-review <level> <pr#>); workflow.run_id and workflow.name OTel attributes enable per-run cost tracing; fixed background sessions dropping on sleep/wake; fixed Remote Control commands failing; improved /workflows agent list with wider titles and dedicated time column.

name: wshobson/agents — 37.6K Stars; 88 Plugins, 194 Agents Across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Copilot, and Gemini CLI
hook: wshobson/agents sits at 37.6K stars as the only plugin marketplace that generates harness-native artifacts from a single Markdown source — one plugin definition deploys correctly to Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI rather than producing a lowest-common-denominator translation. 88 plugins contain 194 domain-expert agents, 158 skills, and 106 commands covering backend, frontend, infrastructure, data, ML, and product workflows. Ships with PluginEval — a quality framework running static checks, LLM judge evals, and Monte Carlo testing on each plugin. Uses a tiered model strategy: Fable 5 for fully autonomous design/architecture tasks; Haiku for high-frequency operational tasks.

name: Graphify — 74.8K Stars; PostgreSQL Live Schema Introspection and Streamable HTTP MCP Transport Added
hook: Graphify continues at ~1 release/day velocity since its YC S26 launch. New this week in v0.8.35+: live PostgreSQL schema introspection (the knowledge graph now auto-refreshes when your schema changes, not just on manual re-index), Streamable HTTP transport for the MCP server (no more stdio-only for remote deployments), Visual Studio 2022 .slnx solution file support, and CodeBuddy platform compatibility. The core proposition unchanged: parses any codebase into a local queryable knowledge graph via tree-sitter AST with 71.5x average token reduction vs. naive file-by-file reads.

name: Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts — 11.6K Stars; 515 Prompt Strings Extracted from Claude Code Source, Updated Within Minutes of Each Release
hook: Piebald-AI reverse-engineers Claude Code's compiled source to extract every system prompt string, tool description, and sub-agent instruction — all 515 of them as of v2.1.202 (July 6, 2026). The repo updates within minutes of each Claude Code release, making it a real-time window into what Claude Code is actually told before it talks to you: harness reminders, planning agent prompts, CLAUDE.md instructions, WebFetch and Bash tool descriptions, security review scripts, agent creation prompts. A detailed changelog tracks what changed across 228 versions since v2.0.14. At 11.6K stars and 490 commits, it has become the standard tool for understanding and debugging harness behavior.

name: claude-forge — 774 Stars; oh-my-zsh for Claude Code; 11 Agents, 34 Commands, 6-Layer Security Hooks
hook: claude-forge describes itself as 'oh-my-zsh for Claude Code' — a comprehensive add-on framework that, in one install, turns bare Claude Code into a fully-equipped development environment. v3.1.0 (June 30) ships 11 specialist agents (architect, reviewer, tester, debugger, and more), 34 slash commands covering planning, TDD, code review, and release workflows, 25 skill procedures that activate automatically based on task context, and a 6-layer security defense system with pre-commit hooks. Also bundles four MCP server connections: browser automation, documentation lookup, web reading, and Chrome DevTools.

name: cass — 946 Stars; Unified TUI to Search Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider, and 17 More Agent Session Histories
hook: cass (coding-agent-session-search) solves a specific pain: you remember solving a problem in a Claude Code session three weeks ago but can't find it. cass indexes conversation histories from 20+ coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider, Gemini CLI, Goose, OpenCode, and more — into a unified search index with sub-60ms latency via edge n-gram indexing. Optional local semantic search via MiniLM, Snowflake Arctic, or Nomic. Three-pane TUI with syntax highlighting; HTML export with optional AES-256 encryption; multi-machine sync via SSH/rsync; JSON output mode for scripting. Install via Homebrew or curl.

name: Claude Code Routines — Official Cloud-Scheduled Agents; Cron, API Trigger, and GitHub Events
hook: Claude Code Routines puts agents on autopilot — define a prompt once, wire up a trigger, and Claude Code runs autonomously on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure (4 vCPUs, 16GB RAM per agent) against any connected GitHub repo.
